keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox gives Location: Southwest Tibet (Ngari Prefecture) and Area: Not stated; the page describes no frontier, partition or change of extent in 354 years, so one shape stands for the whole life. The kingdom became an important link in trans-Himalayan trade after gold was discovered in Western Tibet (undated).

ledger.note: c. 1265: the kingdom of Mangyül Gungthang is founded in south-west Tibet under Sakya overlordship. Established c. 1265 by a descendant of the Tibetan royal house (founder Bumdegon, 1253-1280 on the infobox); capital Dzongkar, the White Fortress. The year is approximate on the page and the region is the researcher's circle.

ledger.note: 1612-13: the Tsangpa ruler leads an expedition to Ngari (West Tibet) and subjugates Mangyül Gungthang. The Karma Phuntsok Namgyal page: In 1612-13 he led an expedition to Ngari (West Tibet), where Mangyül Gungthang was subjugated; the Tsangpa page: In 1612 and 1613, the Tsangpa ruler subjugated a number of local regimes in West Tibet (it does not name Gungthang there).

notes: Written for ea-06-x on the pointer of the ea-06-b report (counterpart 'Mangyül Gungthang', West Tibetan kingdom, taken by the Tsangpa in 1619) from the Mangyul Gungthang, Tsangpa and Karma Phuntsok Namgyal pages. Cliopatria has no row. The shape is the same circle that the Tibet dossier uses, so that the 1619 gain there and the dissolve here move the same cells. Disagreements: the Mangyül Gungthang infobox ends the kingdom in 1620, the Tsangpa and Karma Phuntsok Namgyal pages in 1619 (this dossier: 1619); the Tsangpa page says Latö and the other regimes were subjugated in 1612-13 without naming Gungthang, the Karma Phuntsok Namgyal page names Gungthang. Not on any page opened: the extent of the kingdom (the infobox gives no area and no predecessor), its rulers and partitions, the end of the Sakya overlordship (Sakya rule ended in 1358, see sakya-regime) and its overlords after that: the page says only that the kings were subject to various Central Asian overlords. The Sakya relation is recorded in sakya-regime as vassal events with counterpart mangyul-gungthang. Counterparts needing dossiers: tibet (exists), sakya-regime (this batch).
